description: Two Finger Gripper: next base version (after Gripper 21 / v315). Of the two plates that sandwich and hold the gears, make ONE plate carry all four posts sticking out; those four posts are the pivots the gripper fingers rotate around, so the other plate just caps them. Also from Jake's review of the latest gripper in the live viewer: both parts (he said 'they should both just have that kind of rounded thing', likely both fingers/links getting the same rounded profile) should share the rounded shape, and they may be connected with a loop; changing the finger/gripper design to make that work is allowed. If 'both' is ambiguous after looking at Gripper 21, pick the reading that simplifies the part count and note it in the reply. Goal: simplify the gripper. Jake (voice, 2026-10-20).
test_instructions: Open the new version in the live viewer: one gear plate has all four pivot posts; the fingers rotate on them.
The paired parts share the rounded shape; part count is equal or lower than Gripper 21.

results.identified_issue: Interpretation: Jake's 'four posts' = Base 14's 2 pivot posts (on the base) + 2 pillars (on the top plate). The finger's J-hook sat over each pivot (Gripper 21), which is why Base 9-14 used C rings instead of running the post through. So getting the posts all the way to the cap required a finger change; the pebble allowed that. 'Both ... rounded thing ... connected with a loop' I read as the finger and its handle-gear sharing a round hub, with the finger looped round the post. Rejected: merging the finger into the handle-gear (would lose the separate yellow finger and the finger would float web_t above the bed, so it couldn't print without supports), and a 4-bar linkage with 2 pivots per finger (more parts, contradicts 'simplify'). If Jake meant the two plates should both be rounded, only top2d/base_outline need changing. Fully parametric in params.json; ring_* and pillar_socket/fit params were removed.
results.summary: Base 15 is ready. The base now carries all four posts, and the top plate is just a flat cap over them. The two pivot posts run full height, and the two corner pillars moved over from the top plate. The fingers pivot on the posts: I changed the finger into Gripper 22, where the hook at the bottom of each finger is replaced by a round loop that goes around its post. The finger and its gear now have the same round hub and both turn on the post. I read 'both' as the finger and its gear. I found no change that removes a part without losing the yellow/black split or support-free printing, so the part count stays at Base 14's 10 printed parts. The parts themselves are simpler: the cap has no rings or pillars, and the gears lose their grooves. All 84 geometry checks pass.
results.detailed_description: Built on Base 14 (v314, the newest Base), in v316_generalist_post_cap. Base: two Ø12 pivot posts, 17.65 mm tall from the base's top face, up through the handle-gear web and the finger's loop and 1.85 mm into the cap. Two Ø8 pillars at ±28/−42 reach the cap's underside. Cap: a flat 4 mm plate with a blind Ø12.3 socket over each post tip (2 mm deep, stopping 0.15 mm short of the floor), 2 countersunk M3 down into the pillars (2.6 pilot, blind), and the pinion access hole as before. The C rings and grooves are removed. Gripper 22: the J-hook is replaced by a ring (loop_r 10, Ø12.5 bore, the same clearance as the gear web) that sits concentric with the gear hub (r 14). I dropped two honeycomb holes that would have cut into the loop. Mating checks, run with the parts turning 0 to 30° and with positive controls: each post clears its gear bore and finger loop at 0.25 mm per side; pushing either part 0.5 mm makes it hit the post; the cap touches the base only at the pillar tops; pushing the cap 0.5 mm either way makes it hit the posts; the cap screws bite the pillars. I checked these in the plan view (pivot_stack) and the side view (drive/base renders). The STS3215 seat and Mount 1 are unchanged from Base 14, and their checks still pass. Hole counts are correct: finger 32, base 7, cap 3. New sliders: loop_r, cap_socket, cap_fit, pillar_floor. Nothing has been printed. Older Grippers (1–21) cover the post and won't fit Base 15. The preview may not flag that yet.

summary: Make the Two Finger Gripper's next base version (after Gripper 21 / v315) have one gear-sandwiching plate carrying all four pivot posts, with the other plate only capping them. Give both fingers the same rounded shape, possibly joined by a loop, reading "both" as whichever choice reduces part count and noting it in the reply.

visual.alt: Base 14 vs Base 15 side sections: Base 15's base carries 2 full pivot posts and 2 pillars, the top plate is a flat cap; plan view of Gripper 22's loop round the post
